deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. The heading reads 'Berechnung eines achromatischen Doppelobjectivs. Nro 1', i.e. computation of an achromatic doublet objective, trial no. 1. The page traces light through the FIRST lens (the crown component) in three colours. It does this twice: paraxially ('formula approximata') and with an exact meridional trigonometric ray trace ('formula exacta') for a marginal ray. Comparing the two gives the longitudinal spherical aberration of the first lens for each colour. The next page continues the trace through the second (flint) component.

FORMULAS.
(1) Paraxial refraction followed by transfer to the next surface:
a' = [n/(n-1)] / ( [1/(n-1)]/a + 1/r ) - h,
equivalently n/(a'+h) = 1/a + (n-1)/r. Here a is the distance of the point of convergence beyond the surface, r the radius, h the separation to the next vertex.
(2) Exact ray trace at one spherical surface. φ is the angle of the ray with the axis, A the angle of incidence, B the angle of refraction:
- sin A = (a-r) sin φ / r
- sin B = sin A / n
- φ' = φ + A - B
- a' = r + r sin B / sin φ' - h
For the glass-to-air surface n is replaced by 1/n.

HYPOTHESIS (design data).
- (n-1)/r = 0.015, r = 34.34413.
- (n-1)/r' = 0.005, r' = 103.03240, log r' = 2.0129738.
- Hence the mean index is n-1 = 0.515162.
- Both centres lie on the same side, so the first lens is a MENISCUS of power about 0.015 - 0.005 = 0.010.
- Thickness h = 2. Air gap to the next lens h' = 0.5. Both are inferred from the subtractions of 2 and 0.5.

The three colours (my identification from the logs):
- 0.2972697, 0.2880562, 0.2790341 = log 1/(n-1), giving n-1 = 0.504350, 0.515162, 0.525964.
- 0.1773483, 0.1804591, 0.1835477 = log n, giving n = 1.50435, 1.515162, 1.525964.
- 0.4746180, 0.4685153, 0.4625818 = log n/(n-1).
- 1.5358525 = log r.

PARAXIAL TRACE (a = infinity).
Surface 1:
- a1 + h = n r/(n-1) = 102.44021, 101.01079, 99.64014.
- Minus h = 2 gives a1 = 100.44021, 99.01079, 97.64014.
- Their logs are 2.0019076, 1.9956824, 1.9896284.
Surface 2 (glass to air, n -> 1/n):
- The formula becomes a2 = [1/(n-1)] / ( [n/(n-1)]/a1 - 1/r' ) - h'.
- [n/(n-1)]/a1 = 0.029696850, 0.029705230, 0.029713480.
- 1/r' = 0.009705684.
- The differences are 0.0199912, 0.0199995, 0.0200078; their logs are 8.3008384, (8.)3010202, (8.)3011993.
- a2 = 99.18164, 97.05904, 95.02432 (paraxial image after lens 1).
- Minus 0.5 gives 98.68164, 96.55904, 94.52432 (distances measured from the second lens).

EXACT TRACE.
The incident ray is parallel, with angle of incidence A = 18° at surface 1 (ray height r sin 18° ≈ 10.6).
Surface 1:
- log sin A = 9.4899824.
- Minus log n gives log sin B = 9.3126341, 9.3095233, 9.3064347.
- B = 11°51'13.850", 11°46'4.909", 11°41'0.436".
- φ' = 18° - B = 6°8'46.150", 6°13'55.099", 6°18'59.564".
- log(r sin B) = 0.8484866, 0.8453758, 0.8422872.
- log sin φ' = 9.0296475, 9.0356462, 9.0414769.
- r sin B / sin φ' = 65.89297, 64.52524, 63.21357.
- Plus r gives 100.23710, 98.86937, 97.55770.
- Minus h = 2 gives a1 = 98.23710, 96.86937, 95.55770.
Surface 2 (r' = 103.03240):
- log|a1 - r'| = 0.6808158, 0.7897943, 0.8735938. Here a1 - r' is negative: -4.7953, -6.1630, -7.4747.
- Add log sin φ' and the complement 7.9870262 = -log r'.
- log|sin A| = 7.6974895, 7.8124667, 7.9020969.
- Plus log n gives log|sin B| = 7.8748378, 7.9929278, 8.0856446.
- |A| = 0°17'7.818", 0°22'19.352", 0°27'26.367".
- |B| = 0°25'46.205", 0°33'49.364", 0°41'52.331".
- |B| - |A| = 0°8'38.387", 0°11'30.012", 0°14'25.964".
- φ'' = φ' + A - B = 6°17'24.537", 6°25'25.111", 6°33'25.528".
- log|r' sin B| = 9.8878116, 0.0059016, 0.0986184.
- log sin φ'' = 9.0396656, 9.0487485, 9.0576402.
- Quotients = 7.04930, 9.060519, 10.989506, all taken negative.
- a2 = 103.03240 minus these = 95.98310, 93.97188, 92.04289.
- Minus 0.5 gives 95.48310, 93.47188, 91.54289. These are carried forward on the next page.

CONCLUSIONS (implicit; mine).
- Marginal minus paraxial focus = -3.199, -3.087, -2.981. This is the longitudinal spherical undercorrection of the crown meniscus, slightly colour dependent.
- The paraxial chromatic spread is 99.18 - 95.02 = 4.16.
- The flint lens computed on the next page must cancel both.
- The assumed dispersion, Δn/(n-1) ≈ 0.042, is very large, suggesting fictitious trial glasses.
- The context fits Gauss's 1817 study of doublets corrected for spherical aberration in two colours (meniscus-type 'Gauss objective').
- The crossed-out logs 9.0198901, 9.0221912, 9.0246808 were a first, discarded attempt at log sin φ''. A plausible explanation is that he subtracted (B-A) instead of adding; this is uncertain.
- The footnote '*24,537' re-clarifies the overwritten seconds of 6°17'24.537".
errors: Middle column: 18° - 11°46'4.909" = 6°13'55.091", but Gauss writes 6°13'55.099" and uses it consistently (also on the next page). Either B was really 11°46'4.901" and miscopied, or a subtraction slip of 0.008". Either way it is numerically negligible.
First attempt at log sin φ'' at surface 2 (9.0198901 etc.) was struck out and replaced. It was corrected on the page, so no error propagates.
No substantive errors found. All checked logarithms, angle sums and distances agree to the precision of 7-place tables.

results.what: Paraxial refraction-and-transfer formula a' = (n/(n-1))/((1/(n-1))/a + 1/r) - h, applied to a thick meniscus in three colours
results.modern_name: Paraxial (Gaussian) ray trace / refraction equation n'/s' - n/s = (n'-n)/r with transfer
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-c. optics (Huygens, Euler, Lagrange); systematised by Gauss 1841 Dioptrische Untersuchungen

results.what: Exact meridional trigonometric ray trace: sin A=(a-r)sinφ/r, sin B=sin A/n, φ'=φ+A-B, a'=r+r sinB/sinφ'-h
results.modern_name: Exact meridional (trigonometric) ray tracing through spherical surfaces
results.usually_credited_to: 18th-century (Euler, Klügel and others); standard in lens design thereafter

results.what: Numerical evaluation of longitudinal spherical aberration (~3.1 units at 18° incidence) and chromatic focal spread of the crown meniscus, as step 1 of designing a doublet corrected in several colours
results.modern_name: Spherochromatism / design of a two-meniscus 'Gauss objective'
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss, 'Über die achromatischen Doppelobjective…', Zeitschrift für Astronomie 4 (1817)

deep.surprise_reason: These are working computations for Gauss's known and published 1817 investigation of achromatic doublets corrected for spherical aberration in more than one colour. The ray-trace formulas were standard; only the specific trial numbers are unpublished.
